terms.comment: A country takes a preposition: in Algarbiam (to), in Algarbiā (in), ex Algarbiā (from).

evidence: Mel. 3.1.6: Cuneus ager dīcitur (Lewis & Short s.v. Cuneus)
Graesse, Orbis Latinus (1861), index s.v. Algarve: Cuneus ager
terms.comment: Mela’s name for the wedge of land nearest the Anas (Guadiana), after the promontory Cuneus, the southernmost point of Portugal (Mel. 3.1.6; Plin. 4.116, Lewis & Short). It is a part of the modern Algarve, not the whole.

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio, geographical section, with the authorities it cites (cited as M-O s.v.).

J. G. Th. Graesse, Orbis Latinus (Dresden, 1861), German–Latin index, read in the scan at archive.org (the 1909 edition at columbia.edu could not be reached page by page); its forms are post-classical unless Lewis & Short has them.
